extras.source: Read from each brand's ads by hand (research/<brand>/concepts.md) and from each brand's website (research/<brand>/site.md, both read 23 Nov 2026). Atomberg's sample is the first 30 of about 308 live ads; Qubo's is 42 of about 72. Compare shares, not counts.

A.text: The ₹1,500 fan saving is "every season" in one caption, "per year" on the box and in the ad text, "every year" in a headline over a video that never says it, and has no period in the speech.
The pedestal saving is "every season" in the ad text and "every summer" on the card, and one voice drops "up to" and says a flat ₹400. No page read on the site gives ₹400.

The Intellon promises a 2-year unconditional warranty, 2 years with no service cost, no AMC, zero maintenance and the lowest maintenance costs, in different ads, with no terms shown; the site says a 2-year "No Service Cost" warranty.

The Intellon's saving is 2X more water saving in one ad, about 25,000 rupees over 8 years in another (the site's figure), a litres-a-day usage chart in a third and up to ₹13,000 on the image ad, a figure on no page read.
The smart lock ad text says 6 ways of unlocking; the box shows five icons and the voice names four. The SL 1 page lists six.

B.text: The lock cards say 3 Years Warranty with no asterisk in one pair of ads and 2+ Years Warranty with starred free installation and unstated terms in another; the Select page says 2 years.
AI Guard is said to be built in free while the app frame reads AI Guard Pro Current Plan with an Upgrade button; the cameras page says the features need an active AI Guard plan.
The Q1000 is about 1000 sq ft in a caption and the ad text, 600 m3 per hour and 19,900 only by voice (the product page lists ₹19,990), with a blurred figure in the sister ad.

The dashcam ads name 2K to 4K, front 2K and back HD, 2K + 1080P and a 3K model across three landing pages, with a ₹6,490 deal that has no end date (the page lists ₹6,990) and a heat risk called completely zero.
The doorbell ads give a 4.5 rating from 700+ customers and free installation in 70+ cities, or a lowest price of INR 5990, only in text no video shows; the product page lists ₹8,990 on 23 Nov.

comparable.title: Water purifier against air purifier, and other like for like
comparable.lede: Atomberg's Intellon cleans drinking water; Qubo's Q200 and Q1000 clean room air. They are different products, so neither is in the lock map above. These are the things the two purifier pushes, and the two samples, can fairly be set side by side on.

A.text: The Intellon water purifier: 10 of 30 ads across 9 ideas; 4 are a person to camera, 3 of them on service visits and bills.

B.text: Air purifiers: 9 of 42 ads across 5 ideas; the smoke demo carries 5, and 3 are presenters on room size, auto mode or the Don't buy list.

A.text: Service bills as the doubt to answer: the technician series, 4 ads up to 242 days, shows each filter's health in the app; one ad says about 25,000 rupees saved over 8 years.

B.text: Filters as a sarcastic aside: "filter saste mein aur aasaani se mil jaata hai" is reason three of the Don't buy list; the smoke demo shows a dirty filter.

A.text: None of 30 ads shows a price; the only money figures are savings.

B.text: 5 of 42 show or state one: ₹3,490 and ₹7,990 on images, INR 5990 and ₹6,490 in text, 19,900 said aloud.

A.text: No ad offers free installation; the site offers it in select pincodes.

B.text: 8 of 42 ads say free installation: six lock ads and two doorbell ads.

A.text: 28 distinct videos and images behind 30 ads and 35 versions: nearly every ad is its own creative.

B.text: 31 distinct videos and images behind 42 ads and 54 versions; four lock cards each run as two ads, and the smoke demo as five.
